# **\[v11\_cpe\_lc\] Design Doc — CPE Level Complete UL Migration**

## **1\. Introduction**

### **1.1 Problem Statement**

**Why**: The CPE Level Complete model predicts P(user fires the campaign-targeted SDK event within 7 days of install) and is used to bid on CPE Level Complete campaigns. The current production system runs two separate TensorFlow models in ads-audience-pinpointer:

| Model | Traffic Covered | Identity Type   |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| level\_complete\_bhv | Behavioral | IDFA-identified users only |
| level\_complete\_ctx | Contextual | IDFI \+ unspecified users |

These legacy models have several limitations that motivate migration to the Unified Learner framework: 

1. **No active maintenance**: CPE LC is the ONLY remaining model in   
      ads-audience-pinpointer running TensorFlow. The rest of the UV model   
      family has fully migrated to PyTorch \+ ads-unified-learner, keeping   
      CPE LC in TF creates an isolated maintenance burden with no dedicated   
      resource.  
2. **Split traffic**: BHV handles IDFA only; CTX handles IDFI/unspecified.  
      A unified model trained on all segments can learn cross-segment   
      patterns and simplify serving.  
3. **Stochastic labels**: Legacy samples one SDK event per training step   
      from a ragged label array → non-deterministic, non-reproducible.  
4. **Fragmented infrastructure**: 2 Kubeflow pipelines \+ 2 TFRecord pipelines  
      \+ 2 TF Hub SavedModel deployments → replaced by 1 workflow.

For more details on CPE campaigns, please refer to [Understanding Event Optimaztion Models](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1AI_HzvMuilbOz5kynasjk1IJpn7h2MIlZYbxVVh17Vg/edit?usp=sharing)

### **1.2 Success Criteria**

The v11\_cpe\_lc model unifies BHV+CTX traffic and replaces the TensorFlow framework. Beyond key business metrics, we expect:

| Criterion | Target   |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Performance on CPE LC campaigns** | Neutral-to-positive business metrics vs. legacy BHV \+ CTX combined |
| **Per-SDK-event Bias** | prob\_sdk\_event\_name\_label predictions match observed event-specific conversion rates. Model bias and Product bias are improved |
| **Broader game coverage** | 13,321 distinct target games vs. 1,512 in legacy (\~8.8x), including BHV/CTX combined and campaign table migration |
| **Infrastructure simplification** | One pipeline, one model, one Triton deployment replaces two TF Hub deployments |

## **2\. Data Overview**

### **2.1 Data Source**

| Property | Value |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Source path** | gs://unity-ads-dd-ds-prd-data-anon/app-events/data/ads.events.operativeecpm.installs.outcomes.v2/level\_complete/d7/ |
| **Partition key** | installDate=YYYY-MM-DD |
| **Training window** | 60 days |
| **Label window** | 7 days (app\_event\_w1 \> 0\) |
| **Overall pipeline delay** | 9 days (7-day label \+ 2-day delay) |
| **Preprocessed output** | gs://unity-ads-dd-ds-prd-incremental-training-data/user\_value/unified\_user\_value.v11\_cpe\_lc/preprocessed\_combined/ |

**Row expansion design:** Unlike legacy models (one row per install), the new datagen explodes each install by sdk\_event\_name target: one row per (install × targeted SDK event):

```sql
install_A targeting [level_5, level_10]
└─► Row 1: install_A × level_5
└─► Row 2: install_A × level_10

install_B no specific target → "*" wildcard
└─► Row 1: install_B × "*"
```

This converts ragged array labels into scalar per-row labels, enabling native DLRM compatibility.

### **2.2 Label Design**

Two labels are produced per row:

| Label | Definition | Positive Rate   |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **label** | app\_event\_w1 \> 0 — any level complete within 7 days. Present in parquet but not used as a training target (LC auxiliary task removed). | \~38% (post-quality-filter)  |
| **Prob\_sdk\_event\_name\_label (psn\_label)** | 1.0 if user fired the specific campaign-targeted SDK event AND app\_event\_w1 \> 0, else 0.0. Primary training target and bidding signal. | \~14% (post-fix dataset) |

**Joint distribution** :

| label | psn\_label | Row fraction | Interpretation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 0 | 0 | 61.84% | Non-converters |
| 1 | 0 | 32.9% | Converted but did not fire the specific targeted event |
| 1 | 1 | 14.25% | Converted AND fired the targeted event |

### 

### **2.3 Game-Level Quality Gate**

Mirrors the legacy ads-audience-pinpointer eligibility filter: Keep only games with \>= 50 positive event labels within the past 88 days.

```py
# Keep only games with >= 50 installs having cum_app_event_count_d7 > 0
eligible_game_ids = (
  df.filter(col("cum_app_event_count_d7") > 0)
    .groupBy("targetGameId")
    .agg(count("*").alias("_event_gamers"))
    .filter(col("_event_gamers") >= 50)
)
```

### 

### **2.4 Label Distribution**

**Wildcard '\*' Event Positive Rate**  
**![][image1]**  
Wildcard (\*) event means the game has either an empty or multiple target goals in its campaigns.  
For wildcard rows in UL: prob\_sdk\_event\_name\_label \== label \== (app\_event\_w1 \> 0).   
The model is taught to predict the game's overall level\_complete rate (26.10%) for these rows.  
Its positive rate is way higher than that of only one target event (26.1% vs 14.3%), which leads the model to over-predict on those wildcard campaigns.

**Per- (game, event) Positive Rate Distributions**  
**![][image2]**![][image3]  
The target event label (psn label) showed a long tail distribution, but not all event labels do.

**2.5 Online Bidding Gate — Eligibility Requirement**

Before a game can run a Level Complete campaign, it must have sent us Level Complete events within the last 60-day time window and passed Quality Gate in section 2.3. 

The model only bids on **(target\_game\_id, sdk\_event\_name)** combinations it was trained on with at least one positive PSN label. Combinations never seen in training produce a zero bid.

**How the gate works:**

```shell
Training time (update_mappings step in workflow)
─────────────────────────────────────────────────
  For every (target_game_id, sdk_event_name) pair in the preprocessed
  parquet that has >= 1 row with psn_label=1:
    → write "{target_game_id}_{sdk_event_name}": 1.0
      to trained_game_sdk_combo.json (GCS)

Serving time (DeployModel.forward)
─────────────────────────────────────────────────
  _gate_tensor[target_game_id_idx, sdk_event_name_idx]
    = 1.0  if combo seen in training with a positive PSN label
    = 0.0  otherwise  →  cost = 0  (no bid placed)

  cost = max_cost × discount_factor × p × gate
                                          ^^^^
                                    zeroes out unseen combos
─────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

**trained\_game\_sdk\_combo.json** example file can be found in: [unity-ads-dd-ds-prd-incremental-training-data/user\_value/unified\_user\_value.v11\_cpe\_lc/trained\_game\_sdk\_combo.json](https://console.cloud.google.com/storage/browser/_details/unity-ads-dd-ds-prd-incremental-training-data/user_value/unified_user_value.v11_cpe_lc_v2/trained_game_sdk_combo.json;tab=live_object?pageState=\(%22StorageObjectListTable%22:\(%22f%22:%22%255B%255D%22\)\)&project=unity-ads-dd-ds-prd) 

Example:

```json
  "500037794_af_level14": 1.0,
  "500037795_af_level11": 1.0,
  "500037795_af_level14": 1.0,
  "500037795_af_level20": 1.0,
  "500037795_af_level30": 1.0,
  "500035432_*": 1.0,  --> Game has either empty or multiple target event in campaign settings

```

## **3\. Model Overview**

### **3.1 Model Card**

The technical specifications and configuration for the **unified\_user\_value.v11\_cpe\_lc** model can be found in [this Model Card](https://github.com/yaboling/agent-docs-hub/blob/main/level-complete-migration/doc/model_card_unified_user_value_v11_cpe_lc.md). 

**Serving mechanisms** (both mirror legacy LevelCompleteCostWrapper):

| Mechanism | Description | Source File   |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Mechanism 1 — Eligibility gate | Zeros bid for (target\_game\_id, sdk\_event\_name) combos that the model was never trained on  | [trained\_game\_sdk\_combo.json](https://console.cloud.google.com/storage/browser/_details/unity-ads-dd-ds-prd-incremental-training-data/user_value/unified_user_value.v11_cpe_lc/trained_game_sdk_combo.json;tab=live_object?pageState=\(%22StorageObjectListTable%22:\(%22f%22:%22%255B%255D%22\)\)&project=unity-ads-dd-ds-prd) |
| Mechanism 2 — Product accuracy calibration | Per-campaign correction factor (observed\_rate / predicted\_rate) baked into model artifact at deploy time. Factors clamped to \[0.05, 1.0\] — only shrinks predictions, never inflates. | [product\_accuracy\_calibration.json](https://console.cloud.google.com/storage/browser/_details/unity-ads-dd-ds-prd-incremental-training-data/user_value/unified_user_value.v11_cpe_lc/product_accuracy_calibration.json;tab=live_object?project=unity-ads-dd-ds-prd) |

**Feature engineering highlights:**

> * **Dropped:** UUPS IAP/adrev signals (27 features), IBT embeddings (208-dim), hardware stats scalars/categoricals  
> * **Added:** ad\_format (interstitial vs. rewarded), creative\_id, creative\_pack\_id, device\_orientation, video\_orientation, sdk\_event\_name as sparse embedding  
> * **Unified:** gamer\_id\_scope as a sparse feature lets one model serve both BHV (IDFA) and CTX (IDFI) traffic without separate models

### **3.2 Offline Results**

Offline evaluation was conducted on a 60-day dataset (install dates 2026-02-26 → 2026-04-26, 486M train rows / 18.7M val rows). Model artifact: vny2xtis3e.

Note on metric comparability: Direct loss comparison with legacy is not valid — different label definitions (CPE \~19.75% positive vs. CPI \~37%), different loss formulations (uncertainty-weighted multi-task vs. single-task BCE), different train/val splits.

| Metric | v11\_cpe\_lc (test) | Legacy BHV (train) | Legacy CTX (train)   |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| AUC | 0.9483 | 0.8997 | 0.8991 |
| BCE | 0.3021 | 0.3308 | 0.3313 |
| NE (window) | 0.4119 | \~0.505 | \~0.506 |
| mean\_pred vs mean\_label | bias \< 0.0001 | bias=0.0025 | bias=0.0031 |

**Key takeaways:**

> * Strong AUC gain (+5.4pp vs. legacy) and near-perfect calibration on training data.  
> * Train-only AUC is not directly comparable to legacy val AUC — separate held-out time-based evaluation is required for production go/no-go.

### **4.1 Executive Summary**

v11-cpe-lc-4 passes all scale guardrails and delivers clear wins on both scale and quality. Net Revenue nearly doubles (+99.4%) on Level Complete campaigns. All-traffic Net Revenue is up \+0.71% with a statistically significant positive CI.

### **4.2 Performance Breakdown**

#### **4.2.1 Scale Metrics (All Traffic)**

Source: [EP Business Metrics Report](https://cloud.unity.com/home/admin/experiments/4f4ee12f-e4c4-d53d-b77b-4a5199a9986b/analysis)

| Metric | Lift | 95% CI | Significance   |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Impressions | \+0.14% | (+0.08%, \+0.20%) | ✅ Positive |
| Clicks | \+0.13% | (+0.04%, \+0.22%) | ✅ Positive |
| Installs | −0.11% | (−0.17%, −0.05%) | ⚠️ Slightly negative |
| Publisher Revenue | \+0.30% | (+0.23%, \+0.37%) | ✅ Positive |
| Advertiser Spend | \+0.44% | (+0.23%, \+0.66%) | ✅ Positive |
| Net Revenue | \+0.71% | (+0.15%, \+1.29%) | ✅ Positive |

The slight install dip (−0.11%) reflects the model redistributing budget toward higher-CPE Level Complete campaigns rather than maximizing raw install volume — consistent with the LC optimization objective.

#### **4.2.2 Scale Metrics (Level Complete Traffic Only)**

Source: prediction table (mz\_dcpi\_prediction\_v1) joined to outcome table (operativeecpm\_installs\_outcomes\_contextual) and Campaign table. ([Notebook link](https://colab.research.google.com/drive/1jAaYI7Ep5iY-K1ad50mZNN5_VXIWcxNp?usp=sharing))

**Absolute metrics (normalized to 100% traffic)**:

| Metric | Control (bhv1p \+ ctx1r) | Test (v11-cpe-lc-4) | Delta   |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Starts | 112,344,030 | 144,719,720 | ✅ **\+28.8%** |
| Installs | 531,098 | 768,770 | ✅ **\+44.8%** |
| Spend | $742,042 | $1,305,386 | ✅ **\+75.9%** |
| Net Revenue | $270,153 | $538,731 | ✅ **\+99.4%** |
| eCPI | $1.40 | $1.70 | ⚠️ **\+21.5%** |

The eCPI increase (+21.5%) is expected: the test model serves higher-CPE campaigns and a broader user population (IDFA \+ IDFI \+ unspecified), so cost per install is naturally higher while delivering far greater absolute value.

#### **4.2.3 Post-Install Metrics \- Level Complete Rate**

D0/D1 fully mature. D3 mature through 2026-06-05. D7 mature through 2026-05-31 only.

**Level Complete Rate Dx — any event** (sum\_lc\_label\_dx / installs):

| Window | Control | Test | Delta |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| D0 | 33.06% | 28.48% | ⚠️**−4.58%** |
| D1 | 34.69% | 29.38% | ⚠️**−5.31%** |
| D3 | 35.96% | 30.22% | ⚠️**−5.74%** |
| D7 | 36.35% | 31.01% | ⚠️**−5.34%** |

Lower per-install rate is a composition effect: the unified model serves IDFI and unspecified segments with inherently lower per-install event rates. The absolute number of LC events is \~40% higher for the test arm due to \+44.8% install scale.

**Level Complete Rate Dx — target event** (sum\_target\_lc\_label\_dx / installs):

| Window | Control | Test | Delta |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| D0 | 22.79% | 16.10% | ⚠️**−6.69%** |
| D1 | 22.49% | 15.88% | ⚠️**−6.61%** |
| D3 | 21.84% | 15.36% | ⚠️**−6.48%** |
| D7 | 20.71% | 14.30% | ⚠️**−6.41%** |

The per-install LC rate is lower for the test model. However, the near-perfect product bias on target events indicates the test model is more precisely targeting the advertiser's goal, not merely acquiring users who happen to level-complete.

#### **4.2.3 Accuracy**

D0/D1 fully mature. D3 mature through 2026-06-05. D7 mature through 2026-05-31 only.

**Product Bias — Any Event** ((sum\_cost / sum\_lc\_label\_dx) / avg\_tcpe − 1);

| Window | Control | Test | Verdict |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| D0 | \-0.49 | \-0.47 | ≈ Comparable |
| D1 | \-0.50 | \-0.49 | ≈ Comparable |
| D3 | \-0.50 | \-0.51 | ≈ Comparable |
| D7 | \-0.48 | \-0.49 | ≈ Comparable |

Both models show similar product bias on any-event CPE (\~−50%), reflecting the expected gap between same-day cost allocation and cumulative D7 attribution. 

**Product Bias — Target Event** ((sum\_cost / sum\_target\_lc\_label\_dx) / avg\_tcpe − 1):

| Window | Control | Test | Delta |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| D0 | \-0.26 | \-0.07 | ✅ Test 3.5x closer to target |
| D1 | \-0.25 | \-0.06 | ✅ Test 4x closer to target |
| D3 | \-0.23 | \-0.02 | ✅ Text 11x closer to target |
| D7 | \-0.18 | \+0.05 | ✅ Partial outcome |

**This is the strongest signal in the experiment.** The test model delivers the campaign-specific target event at a cost almost exactly matching the advertiser's target CPE (−7% to \+5% across D0–D7), while the legacy control consistently underpredicts by 18–26%. Near-zero product bias on target events means advertisers receive the exact events they targeted at the price they set.

## **Appendix**

### **A.1 Model Offline Evaluation \- Removing Creative Level Features**

**Summary**: The test model (no creative features) is effectively equivalent to the baseline in discriminative power: GINI drops by only \-0.16%, which is negligible at this scale. However, it clearly outperforms on calibration (1.21% → 0.45% over-prediction), through shifting the over-prediction to under-prediction in low-to-mid probability bins.

Both models share the same structural weakness: significant over-prediction in the highest probability bin (B9, \~+0.012), which is unaffected by removing creative features and likely requires dedicated calibration work.

Offline Details: [offline\_eval\_comparison\_executed.ipynb](https://colab.research.google.com/drive/1hr7y1Svc9xVsJMzibGfpe3Z2Zop-cA8Z?usp=sharing)  
Removed Features: ad\_format, video\_orientation, creative\_id, creative\_pack\_id, ad\_type

#### **A.1.1 Overall Metrics**

| Metric | Baseline | Test | Δ abs | Δ% |
| :---- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| BCE | 0.302129 | 0.302117 | \-0.000013 | \-0.004% |
| AUC | 0.826875 | 0.826343 | \-0.000532 | \-0.064% |
| GINI | 0.65375 | 0.652686 | \-0.001064 | \-0.163% |
| Model Bias ((y\_pred / y\_true)  \- 1\) | 0.012093 | 0.004484 | \-0.007609 | \-62.9% |

**Discriminative power (AUC/GINI)**: Near-neutral, slight regression

* GINI drops by only \-0.163%, well within noise range for a model of this scale. Removing creative-level features did not meaningfully hurt the model's ability to rank predictions. This suggests creative features were not providing much incremental signal for discrimination.


**Calibration (Bias)**: Clear winner for Test model

* Bias drops from \+1.21% to \+0.45%, a \-62.9% reduction in over-prediction. The test model is substantially better calibrated. This is the most meaningful difference between the two models.

**BCE**: Essentially identical

* 0.004% change is negligible.

#### **A1.2 Per-Event GINI Breakdown (947 events with n≥200)**

| Metric | Count |
| :---- | ----- |
| Events where Test GINI improved | 459 (48.5%) |
| Events where Test GINI degraded | 488 (51.5%) |
| Median GINI delta | \-0.0022 |
| Mean GINI delta | \+0.0030 |

The split is nearly 50/50, with both median and mean close to zero. The large individual swings (e.g. `500187386_level_end_success_30`: **\+0.527**, `500000421_d7_puzzle65_ltv300cents`: **\-0.496**) are almost certainly noise from small sample sizes (n\~200-700) rather than systematic effects of removing creative features.

**Top 20 (game, target\_event) GINI Increase & Decrease**

#### **A1.3 Calibration curve: prediction vs label bucketed into 10 bins**

| Bin range | Baseline | Test |
| :---- | ----- | ----- |
| B0–B4 (low pred) | Near-zero, slight under-pred (−0.0001 to −0.0006) | Clear under-pred (−0.0004 to −0.0027) |
| B5–B8 (mid-high pred) | Consistent over-pred (+0.0012 to \+0.0017) | Slight over-pred (+0.0007 to \+0.0027) |
| B9 (highest pred) | Large over-pred (+0.0124) | Large over-pred (+0.0128) |

Both models are large over-predicting in the highest probability bin (\~+0.012). In the mid-range behaviour, the test model shows a lower over-prediction issue.
